channel.title: AI News Digest
channel.description: Official AI product updates from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and GitHub

item.title: Responding to the next frontier of critical cyber capabilities
item.description: OpenAI is sharing preliminary cybersecurity evaluations for Astra and the steps we’re taking to strengthen safeguards and security controls.

item.title: How HSP GRUPPE builds AI capabilities for tax advisory
item.description: Discover how HSP GRUPPE uses ChatGPT Enterprise to boost productivity, improve work quality, and create more capacity for tax advisory and client service.

item.title: Secret scanning coverage updates
item.description: This release expands secret scanning’s coverage with more secrets blocked by push protection, one new secret scanning partner, and richer metadata on alerts. Secret scanning partnership program Lovable Labs is now a GitHub secret scanning partner.

item.title: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 3
item.description: This week’s updates across GitHub Copilot in the desktop app, CLI, and VS Code help you resume and organize work, review changes, and ask questions without losing context. GitHub Copilot app Auto now shows which model handled each completed request, plus AI credit and cache details when they’re available.

item.title: GitHub Code Quality no longer adds Copilot as a reviewer
item.description: Enabling GitHub Code Quality on a repository no longer creates a ruleset that automatically requests a code review from GitHub Copilot on your pull requests. In repositories that already have that ruleset, we’ve turned off the settings we enabled.

item.title: Copilot usage metrics API adds agent app activity
item.description: Since agent apps arrived on GitHub, teams have been able to run agents from partners like Claude and Codex directly in their GitHub workflows. The Copilot usage metrics API now reports that activity, broken out by individual agent.

item.title: Copilot impact dashboard adds a return on investment section
item.description: The Copilot impact dashboard now includes a “Potential return on investment” section that connects what you spend on Copilot to the pull request output you get back. What’s new Two cards compare developers by how deeply they have adopted Copilot: those working primarily in chat and code completions (i.e., “Passive users” and “Phase 1”) against agent-first developers (i.e., “Phase 2” and “Phase 3”).

item.title: Copilot code review effort levels are generally available
item.description: Lite and Balanced effort levels for GitHub Copilot code review are now generally available. They let you match the depth of a review to the complexity and risk of a pull request.

item.title: MCP allowlists in enterprise managed settings
item.description: Enterprise owners can now centrally control which Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers GitHub Copilot clients are allowed to run by using the new allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers keys in enterprise managed settings. Approve the MCP servers your developers depend on and block untrusted or non-compliant ones across your enterprise.

item.title: .claude/skills
item.description: Claude Managed Agents sessions can now load skills from a GitHub repository. When a session mounts a repository, any skills in its root.claude/skills directory are discovered automatically at session start and available to the agent for that session.

item.title: {"type": "advisor"}
item.description: You can now give a Claude Managed Agents session an advisor: a model at least as capable as the agent's own that the session's primary thread can consult mid-turn for strategic guidance. Configure it as a {"type": "advisor"} entry in the agent's multiagent roster, naming the model to consult. See Give the session an advisor.

item.title: Improving Fable 5 Safeguards
item.description: We’re making updates to Claude Fable 5’s biology safeguards in a way that substantially reduces fallbacks.

item.title: budget_reached
item.description: You can now set a budget on a Claude Managed Agents session: a hard cap on the session's spend, priced at public list rates. A session that reaches its budget pauses with the budget_reached stop reason instead of starting new model requests; changing or removing the budget resumes it. Deployments accept the same budget and apply it to each session they start. See Session budgets.

item.title: inference_geo
item.description: You can now control where model inference runs for a Claude Managed Agents agent. Set inference_geo inside the model object when you create the agent, or override it for a single session. See Data residency for the available geos and pricing.

item.title: Working with the American Psychological Association on youth mental health and AI
item.description: OpenAI and the American Psychological Association advance evidence-based guidance, resources, and safeguards for responsible AI use and youth mental health.

item.title: Improving GPT‑5.6 Sol in ChatGPT—and expanding access to GPT-5.6 Luna for free users
item.description: ChatGPT introduces improved GPT-5.6 Sol with better accuracy and consistency, plus expanded access for free users and unlimited everyday chats with GPT-5.6 Luna.

item.title: From asking to doing: How the world is putting ChatGPT to work
item.description: New OpenAI Signals data shows how people use ChatGPT worldwide, with country-level insights on adoption, usage trends, and evolving behavior.

item.title: Kimi K3 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Editor’s note (August 6, 2026): We have resumed rolling out Kimi K3 in GitHub Copilot. This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing.

item.title: Fast mode, pricing details
item.description: Fast mode now supports long-context requests for GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, and GPT-5.6 Luna. As of today, long-context prompts exceeding 272K tokens can run in Fast mode, delivering speeds up to 2.5× faster than the Standard tier.

item.title: Inference hooks
item.description: Inference hooks are now in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations. Point Claude at your organization's AI security server, and each governed prompt across claude.ai, Cowork, and Claude Code is held for the server's allow or deny verdict before inference proceeds. Requests are signed, failure handling is configurable, and every denial is recorded in the compliance Activity Feed. See Inference hooks.

item.title: Third-party cyber evaluations involving OpenAI models
item.description: OpenAI explains recent third-party cybersecurity evaluation incidents and outlines new safeguards to strengthen AI model testing and evaluation.

item.title: New ways to learn and teach with ChatGPT Work and Codex
item.description: Explore new education plugins for ChatGPT Work and Codex that help K–12 teachers, college educators, and students learn, teach, research, and build.

item.title: The latest AI news we announced in July 2026
item.description: Here are Google’s latest AI updates from July 2026

item.title: Upcoming deprecation of GitHub Spark on github.com
item.description: Beginning August 4, 2026, GitHub Spark no longer accepts new users or allows the creation of new apps. Existing users can continue to access GitHub Spark until August 31, 2026 to export apps they’ve already created.

item.title: Retiring the Copilot Billing Preview app
item.description: We’ve retired the GitHub Copilot Billing Preview app, and it’s no longer available. You can review and manage your Copilot spend directly in your GitHub billing settings.

item.title: Code coverage automatic enablement in Code Quality settings
item.description: We’re making code coverage setup faster and simpler. You’ll now see a new option in your repository’s Code Quality settings that lets GitHub generate your coverage workflow automatically with AI.

item.title: Tino Cuellar joins Anthropic as Chief Global Affairs Officer
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: How we built a realtime system for responsive voice AI in six months
item.description: GPT-Live enables continuous voice interaction with AI, using a turnless speech model and low-latency architecture for faster, more natural conversations.

item.title: Circles powers telco personalization with OpenAI technology
item.description: Circles uses the OpenAI API and Codex to power AI-native telco experiences, increasing ARPU by 22%, reducing churn by 9%, and improving development efficiency.

item.title: Apple is getting this wrong
item.description: OpenAI addresses Apple’s baseless lawsuit, corrects claims about its employees, and shares messages documenting what happened.

item.title: Inside our 353,000-person vibe coding course
item.description: Kaggle’s AI Agents Intensive with Google brought learners together in a no-cost course to build and deploy the next frontier of AI.

item.title: Trigger Copilot automations with comments
item.description: You can now create Copilot cloud agent automations that run when an issue comment or pull request comment is created. Common use cases include: Generate documentation: Comment on a pull request to automatically generate or update documentation based on your code changes.

item.title: Enterprise team specialization for managed settings
item.description: Enterprise administrators can now customize managed settings by targeting enterprise teams with itemized configuration files. Large enterprises can scale governance without bottlenecking every configuration change through central administrators or one-size-fits-all policies.

item.title: Customize the reasoning level for Copilot cloud agent
item.description: When you delegate a task to GitHub Copilot cloud agent, you can now set the reasoning level for models that support it. This allows you to control how much the model reasons before it responds.

item.title: Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science
item.description: OpenAI shares new results on long-standing open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, including advances in geometry, cryptography, and complexity.

item.title: Dreams
item.description: Dreams (research preview) now supports Claude Opus 5. See Supported models.

item.title: Univé builds an AI-ready workforce
item.description: See how Univé built an AI-ready workforce with ChatGPT Enterprise by combining leadership, responsible governance, and employee-led innovation to transform work at scale.

item.title: Disrupting a Criminal Scam Operation
item.description: OpenAI disrupted a Cambodia-based scam operation using ChatGPT to support investment, romance, gambling, and impersonation schemes.

item.title: Building abundant intelligence
item.description: A full-stack approach to making advanced AI more capable, more affordable, and more widely useful.

item.title: Advancing responsible AI across Europe
item.description: OpenAI shares how its safety, security, transparency, and provenance practices support responsible AI governance in Europe. The work will continue as the EU AI Act advances.

item.title: Enterprise teams model policy targeting in public preview
item.description: You can now take advantage of user-based model policy targeting for GitHub Enterprise customers with Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise licenses. This feature empowers AI administrators to set a baseline of models for the entire enterprise and then grant additional models to specific enterprise teams.

item.title: pricing details
item.description: Starting July 30, GPT-5.6 Luna costs 80% less, while GPT-5.6 Terra costs 20% less. See pricing details.

item.title: How avatarin built a 24/7 retail agent with GPT-Realtime
item.description: avatarin uses OpenAI’s GPT-Realtime to give Yamada Denki shoppers 24/7 multilingual support. In two weeks, 30,000 people used the agent and 92% of survey responses were positive.

item.title: Advancing the price-performance frontier with GPT-5.6
item.description: Explore lower GPT‑5.6 pricing for Luna and Terra—and how OpenAI’s more efficient models help enterprises deploy AI workflows at scale.

item.title: Gemini Robotics ER 2: powering robotics with video understanding, task orchestration, and multi-robot collaboration
item.description: Gemini Robotics ER 2 helps robots reason, collaborate, and solve real-world tasks. It represents a step change in video understanding, tool orchestration, and multi-robot collaboration for robotic applications.

item.title: Stacked pull requests are now in public preview
item.description: Stacked pull requests break large changes into small, reviewable pull requests. They’re an ordered series of pull requests that each represent focused layers of your change.

item.title: Limit remote control to managed devices
item.description: Enterprises and organizations can now restrict which devices are eligible to host remotely controlled Copilot sessions, giving administrators fine-grained control over where remote control access is permitted. The new remoteControl enterprise managed setting gives administrators the ability to define exactly how remote control works on managed devices, whether that means requiring SSO authorization for specific organizations or tailoring access on a per-device basis.

item.title: GitHub Models is now retired
item.description: As of July 30, 2026, GitHub Models is now retired. The playground, model catalog, inference API, and bring your own key (BYOK) are no longer available to any customer, including existing customers with active usage.

item.title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — July update
item.description: July 2026 brought a new agent based on the Copilot SDK, built-in expertise from the.NET and Azure teams, and more ways to tailor GitHub Copilot to how you and your team work. Highlights Here’s what’s new with GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio 2026.

item.title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, July 2026 releases
item.description: This changelog covers VS Code v1.127 through v1.131, shipped throughout July 2026. These releases improve how you work with agents, review changes, use chat, and navigate VS Code.
